title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case, not a model failure. A person with legitimate access to law enforcement systems is accused of using them for a purpose they were not built for: locating and following a private individual. The systems named are a camera network, a tag reader network, and a state criminal justice database, all of which exist to support police work and all of which were allegedly turned to a personal end.

The failure sits at the access layer rather than in any model. Each of those systems grants broad query and tracking capability to sworn staff, and the only thing standing between that capability and a private target is the operator's own compliance plus whatever audit trail the agency keeps. Catching this kind of use requires logging that ties every query and camera or tag lookup to a case number or stated purpose, and review that actually reads those logs. Whether Coffee County had such controls, and whether they were what surfaced the conduct, is not established in the reporting.

The reporting describes an indictment and an arrest, not a conviction. The eight counts are allegations, the bond release is not a finding of guilt, and no court has yet weighed the evidence.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, was released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including stalking and misuse of law enforcement databases. The 49-year-old is accused of using the sheriff's office camera system, tag reader system, and the Georgia Crime Information Center database for personal reasons between April and May 2024. He was terminated when the investigation began.

The woman he allegedly tracked spoke anonymously, saying she hopes her story encourages other women to report abuse. Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. He is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
